text:
Jordan Eberle is 36, in his fifth season in Seattle and his 17th in the league, and he is still doing the same job he's done since Edmonton: get to the dangerous ice and finish. He has 6 goals and 13 points in 19 games, and the goals match his chances almost exactly (6 goals on 6.0 expected). There's no luck to strip out here. That's who he is.

The power play is carrying the line: 8 of his 13 points have come with the extra man. At five on five the picture is harder. Seattle gets about 45% of the shot attempts and expected goals with him on the ice, and his ice time has slipped under 15 minutes in each of the last three games. He was never fast, and the tracking says it: his top speed sits near the bottom eighth of the league.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.0 wins last season, mostly from even-strength offense. What to watch is whether the five-on-five shifts hold up as his minutes shrink, because the power play alone won't keep a winger in the top six.
